title: streaming lifecycle controls: robust client cancel/disconnect handling, reconnect/resume, and server-timeout defaults
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: customer and internal load tests show edge cases where long-lived streaming connections combined with intermittent network drops or client-initiated cancels could leave server-side state (KV caches, request contexts) retained longer than expected, leading to resource pressure and occasional duplicate tool invocations. This PR implements a unified lifecycle control surface for streaming: (1) explicit client-cancel handling that guarantees idempotent cancellation of active request state and best-effort propagation of cancel to downstream tool/function calls, (2) robust disconnect detection and server-side grace windows with configurable reconnect/resume tokens, (3) reconnection/resume semantics for clients with short network blips (OpenAI-compatibility-layer supports resume tokens), and (4) sane server-timeout defaults and per-deployment knobs to avoid indefinite resource retention. Key design points: single-stream lifecycle state machine in runtime connection_manager, resume token encoding that is revocable and short-lived by default, conservative server-side timeouts to free resources (default 30s for unfinished streams after disconnect), and explicit guarantees around at-most-once tool/function calls when resume is attempted. Compatibility: preserves OpenAI compatibility for streaming endpoints while adding optional resume headers and a new resume_token field in the final event payload when resumable, no change to existing non-resumable streams. Rollout plan: behind a feature flag (runtime.streaming.lifecycle.v2) enabled for internal staging, gradual ramp to 25% of traffic, then full rollout after 1 week of telemetry. Migration: SDK updates included for JS and Python; clients that do not opt into resume will see no behavioral change. See linked linear tickets for perf tuning and followups.

review_comments: Ravi Desai: Can you clarify guarantees for tool invocation duplication on resume? The PR notes at-most-once but details are thin.

Ava Martinez (author): Tool calls are wrapped with an idempotency token; on resume we check server-side token cache and short-circuit duplicate invocations. Added comments and tests to make this explicit.
Lin Chen: Suggest lowering the default server-side disconnect grace window to 30s from 60s; we still need to monitor flakiness from mobile clients.
Ava Martinez (author): Lowered default to 30s and made it configurable per-deployment. Updated observability to emit 'stream_disconnect_grace' metric.
Morgan Patel: Integration test flaked once on CI due to timing; can we add a retry or increase clock skew tolerance?
Ava Martinez (author): Increased test timeouts and added a deterministic fake clock for the flaky case.
Ravi Desai: Approving after nit fixes (added more logging around resume token validation).

release_notes:
- Add streaming lifecycle controls: client cancel propagation, disconnect detection, reconnect/resume support with resume_token.
- Default server-side stream disconnect grace window set to 30s (configurable).
- SDK helpers for JS/Python to simplify reconnect+resume flows.
- At-most-once tool/function call semantics on resume via idempotency tokens.
notes_for_ops: Feature is behind runtime.streaming.lifecycle.v2 flag. Start with 5% traffic, monitor 'stream_disconnect_grace' and 'stream_resume_success' metrics, and watch for elevated tool-invocation counts during rollout.
